mismatches.detail: For 'AI Engineer, Community Support Engineering' the listing page (and pipeline output) shows location='China - Remote', while the job's own detail page 'Offices:' field says 'Beijing, China' (no remote qualifier). This reflects a genuine difference between the listing badge and the detail-page field on Airbnb's own site, not a pipeline error — the pipeline correctly transcribed what the listing page shows.

top_observations: All 3 sites required escalation past tier-0 (no JSON-LD job postings on any of them) and past at least one LLM-on-static attempt — consistent with the group definition (no public ATS API, custom JS-heavy front ends). Amazon in particular burned through the full ladder (0->1->2->4, 7 attempts, 238K tokens, 57s) before vision succeeded, because its tier-2 rendered_llm attempts failed even though a plain Playwright render clearly contains the job list — worth investigating whether the tier-2 DOM/a11y serialization is truncating or mis-structuring React-virtualized list content.

When tier-1/tier-2 LLM extraction does succeed, per-field accuracy on the postings it returns is high (Apple 2/2, Amazon 6/6, Airbnb 5/5 correct on title/location; no hallucinated postings on any site) — the failure mode across sites is under-coverage (missing available postings), not fabrication.

Two distinct under-coverage bugs were caught by ground-truthing the exact HTML the model saw: Apple's tier-1 sonnet pass extracted only 2 of 19 postings that were actually present in the fetched static HTML (a clean parser_bug), and Amazon's tier-4 vision pass silently dropped the topmost on-screen job (viewport/scroll-crop parser_bug). Neither would be visible from the CLI's own JSON output alone since 'success' just requires >=1 valid posting.

Robots.txt correctness matters more than expected: Google's careers listing looked plausibly allowed on a naive read of the disallow rules (only ?page= variants are listed under User-agent: *), but urllib.robotparser — and the pipeline itself — both independently disallow the bare URL, so it was excluded rather than force-run.

Pre-run screening eliminated more 'famous' candidates than it kept: Netflix and Microsoft careers are both actually Eightfold.ai-hosted (x-ef-* headers, docs.eightfold.ai in CSP), Nvidia/Meta leak myworkdayjobs.com links, Costco runs on iCIMS+Taleo, Home Depot on Workday+BrassRing, and Walmart/Boeing/Disney disallow their job-search paths in robots.txt — genuinely custom, robots-permitted, ATS-free career sites are the exception, not the rule, among large companies.
